query: How long is an Aether access token valid before it expires?

relevant_chunks.anchor: This short lifetime is a deliberate blast-radius decision

query: What does Aether do when a refresh token is presented a second time after it was already used?

relevant_chunks.anchor: revokes the entire family of sessions descended from that original refresh token

query: How can you tell a development API key apart from a production one just by looking at it?

relevant_chunks.anchor: carries a prefix that encodes which environment it was issued in

query: Does a failed login attempt reveal whether the email address even has an account?

relevant_chunks.anchor: collapses several distinct failure reasons into one identical, indistinguishable error response

query: During a signing-key rotation, how long does the previous key stay valid for verification?

relevant_chunks.anchor: Outside of an active rotation window, only a single signing key is configured at all
This overlap window means a signing-key rotation never has to forcibly invalidate

query: How does Aether know which signing key to check a JWT's signature against if more than one key is valid at once?

relevant_chunks.anchor: the verifying side always knows exactly which key to check a given token's signature against even if multiple keys are valid at once

query: What's notable about the very first successful use of a brand new API key?

relevant_chunks.anchor: the very first successful use of a brand new key, are both the kind of volume and novelty signals

query: What happens to a document that fails Aether's malware scan?

relevant_chunks.anchor: immediately marked as rejected and never proceeds to chunking or embedding

query: What does Aether use to embed chunks when no real embedding provider key is configured?

relevant_chunks.anchor: falls back to a local, deterministic, hash-based embedding scheme

query: What happens to an outbox message that keeps failing and exhausts its delivery attempts?

relevant_chunks.anchor: moved into a dead-letter state rather than being retried forever

query: Can a workspace see documents that failed to ingest when it lists its documents?

relevant_chunks.anchor: includes documents that have failed processing as well as ones still in progress

query: What determines the maximum size Aether will accept for a document upload?

relevant_chunks.anchor: issued with an explicit maximum size baked in at the moment it is created

query: What kind of document ends up retrievable only as a single, undifferentiated chunk?

relevant_chunks.anchor: a document that produces only one chunk because it was too short will only ever be retrievable as a single, undifferentiated unit

query: In what order does the LLM router try configured providers?

relevant_chunks.anchor: OpenAI first if configured, then Anthropic, then Groq

query: How many consecutive failures does it take before a provider's circuit breaker opens?

relevant_chunks.anchor: After three consecutive failures against that specific provider, its breaker opens

query: How long does a provider's circuit breaker stay open before it tries a test call again?

relevant_chunks.anchor: after a cooldown period of thirty seconds it transitions to a half-open state

query: Can the router retry a different provider after it has already started streaming a reply to the client?

relevant_chunks.anchor: Once even one token has reached the client, a mid-stream failure from that provider is surfaced as a real, hard error

query: What happens if a provider is configured with a model name that's absent from that provider's own capability registry?

relevant_chunks.anchor: treated as a startup-time configuration error rather than something silently tolerated at request time

query: For how long does Aether hold the concurrency limit against a provider during one generation?

relevant_chunks.anchor: held for the entire duration of a streaming generation, not just for the moment the request is issued

query: Why does each provider adapter report its own per-model cost figures instead of one shared price?

relevant_chunks.anchor: applying one provider's price to every model it could possibly serve would produce a plausible but wrong number

query: What constant does Aether add to the rank position when fusing the vector and lexical leg rankings?

relevant_chunks.anchor: The constant added to the rank before dividing is set to sixty

query: What weighting does MMR use to balance relevance against diversity when selecting chunks?

relevant_chunks.anchor: The balance between the two signals is controlled by a weighting constant set to one half

query: How does MMR treat a chunk that arrived only through the lexical leg and has no embedding yet?

relevant_chunks.anchor: treated as maximally diverse from everything else rather than excluded

query: What are Gate One and Gate Two in Aether's grounded refusal protocol?

relevant_chunks.anchor: Gate One runs immediately after retrieval and before any call to a language model
Gate Two is enforced by the system prompt handed to the language model

query: How was Aether's retrieval refusal threshold actually calibrated?

relevant_chunks.anchor: setting the threshold to half of the weakest observed score among those genuine positive matches

query: What kinds of failures cause hybrid search to fall back to lexical-only results?

relevant_chunks.anchor: a lost connection, a query that exceeds its timeout, or an index that is temporarily unavailable while being rebuilt

query: What does Aether do if removing a member would leave a workspace with no Owners at all?

relevant_chunks.anchor: actively refuses any action — removing a member, downgrading a role, or leaving a workspace — that would leave a workspace with zero remaining Owners

query: How does Postgres row-level security know which workspace a request is scoped to?

relevant_chunks.anchor: the connection handling a request sets a session-local configuration value identifying which workspace the current request is scoped to

query: What is the purpose of a workspace budget's soft-limit percentage?

relevant_chunks.anchor: does not block any requests by itself; it exists purely as a threshold for surfacing a warning

query: Does resetting a workspace's monthly budget require any action from an administrator?

relevant_chunks.anchor: without any manual intervention or explicit reset action required from an administrator

query: What is the expected, healthy value of Aether's row-level-security violation metric?

relevant_chunks.anchor: this metric's expected value in correct operation is exactly zero at all times

query: What percentage of requests does Aether trace by default?

relevant_chunks.anchor: at least ten percent of requests are traced

query: What happens to tracing when no trace collector endpoint is configured?

relevant_chunks.anchor: falls back to a genuine no-op rather than silently buffering spans that go nowhere

query: What kinds of actions produce an entry in Aether's audit log?

relevant_chunks.anchor: a membership role change, a workspace deletion request, an API key being created or revoked

query: What SLO tier does Aether's demo deployment topology commit to?

relevant_chunks.anchor: explicitly a single-node topology rather than a highly available one, and it is held to a corresponding service level objective tier

query: If document processing keeps failing, does Aether keep retrying the outbox message forever?

relevant_chunks.anchor: moved into a dead-letter state rather than being retried forever

distractor_anchor: Once even one token has reached the client, a mid-stream failure from that provider is surfaced as a real, hard error
notes: Real answer is ingestion's outbox dead-letter behavior. The router's retry-before-first-token rule is a genuinely different retry policy in a different subsystem, but shares enough retry/fallback vocabulary to be a real lexical-leg distractor.

query: Does the router retry a failed generation against a different provider partway through streaming a response?

relevant_chunks.anchor: Once even one token has reached the client, a mid-stream failure from that provider is surfaced as a real, hard error

distractor_anchor: it becomes eligible for another delivery attempt on the worker's next poll
notes: Inverse of near-miss-01: the outbox's retry-on-next-poll behavior is a real, differently-scoped retry policy that shares vocabulary with the router's retry rule.

query: How exactly does Aether compute the pre-request cost estimate used to check a generation against budget limits?

relevant_chunks.anchor: a pre-request admission check using a conservative cost estimate: a local count of the prompt's tokens plus the request's maximum allowed completion tokens

distractor_anchor: a separate, coarser pre-request estimate is computed from a local token count and a conservative worst-case per-thousand-token rate
notes: The workspace-tenancy doc's Budget Admission Control section is the canonical, complete description; the router doc mentions the same underlying mechanism in passing while discussing cost accounting, using very similar wording.

query: What mechanism does Aether use to let a workspace download a completed data export?

relevant_chunks.anchor: made available through the same object-storage-backed, presigned-URL download mechanism documents themselves are uploaded through

distractor_anchor: the client requests a presigned upload URL scoped to a specific object key and a maximum allowed size
notes: Both passages use "presigned URL" — one for upload (ingestion), one for the export's download (tenancy) — real shared terminology across two different directions of the same mechanism.

query: When a workspace owner requests deletion, does the workspace's data get purged immediately as part of that request?

relevant_chunks.anchor: Requesting deletion creates a tracked deletion job and marks the workspace accordingly, after which the workspace's data is actually purged asynchronously

distractor_anchor: a message describing the new document is placed on an outbox for asynchronous processing rather than being processed synchronously as part of the original upload request
notes: Both workspace deletion and document ingestion use the same asynchronous-job pattern, described with overlapping words (asynchronous/synchronously/job/request) in two different docs.

query: Which of Aether's real, live metrics is expected to read exactly zero during normal, healthy operation?

relevant_chunks.anchor: this metric's expected value in correct operation is exactly zero at all times

distractor_anchor: that would leave a workspace with zero remaining Owners
notes: The RLS-violation counter is the real live metric expected to be zero. Workspace ownership's "zero remaining Owners" is a policy rule, not a measured metric, but shares the word "zero" and appears in the same general governance-adjacent vocabulary.

query: Where does Aether track the gap between a request's pre-request cost estimate and its actual settled cost?

relevant_chunks.anchor: the gap between pre-request estimated cost and actual settled cost, which is the signal for whether admission control's conservative estimate is running too far from reality

distractor_anchor: Aether tracks the gap between the two as a deliberate signal for whether its estimation approach is running too conservative or too loose over time
notes: The observability doc's cost dashboard is the more precise answer to "where is this tracked" (a dashboard panel); the tenancy doc describes the same underlying gap-tracking concept in the budgeting mechanism itself.

query: What specific number does Aether use as a cutoff before treating repeated failures as a real, unhealthy problem?

relevant_chunks.anchor: After three consecutive failures against that specific provider, its breaker opens

distractor_anchor: The constant added to the rank before dividing is set to sixty
notes: Circuit breaker's three-failure threshold is the real answer to an unhealthy-provider question. RRF's constant of sixty is an unrelated numeric constant, but both are introduced as "a constant"/"a number" in nearby phrasing, a plausible lexical collision.
